title: Split language build runners + smart cache priming to reduce cross-language cache thrash
creator: Alyssa Park
description: Historic CI runs in our monorepo cause excessive remote cache churn: changes to Docker base layers, node_modules resolution differences, and mixed-language build steps invalidate the cache and lengthen builds. This ticket separates language-specific build runners, introduces a lightweight orchestration layer for slicing the build graph, and implements a smart cache priming/credentialized remote CAS onboarding to reduce cold-cache penalties and stabilize median CI times.
background_and_rationale: Observed median CI time for PRs touching multiple packages: 18m (vs target 8m).
Recent incidents: two rollbacks due to flaky integration builds caused by tooling changes in the Node runner (see INC-2026-04).

Current root causes: shared Docker base updates invalidating all builders; monolithic runner images with language toolchains installed indiscriminately; poor cache key hygiene across language boundaries; no consistent cache priming after base image updates.
acceptance_criteria: CI median PR build time reduced to <= 9 minutes on typical change sets (non-large monorepo changes).
Cache hit rate on remote CAS increases by >= 30% within two weeks of rollout for cross-language PRs.
Build failures due to toolchain mismatch reduced to near-zero for Node/Python projects after runner split.
Documentation describing how to onboard new language runners and how to add priming hooks is published in Confluence.
E2E smoke that validates artifact compatibility across runner boundaries exists and runs in nightly builds.
tasks: Design orchestration: define graph slice boundaries and dependency graph API (owner: Diego)
Implement language runner prototypes: node-runner, python-runner, go-runner, rust-runner (owner: Priya)
Introduce builder image versioning and base-layer pinning strategy + template images (owner: Infra)
Add credentialized remote CAS client to runners and implement secure token rotation (owner: Security)
Implement cache-priming job that runs after base-image patch merges and primes hot prefixes (owner: CI)
Update lint/toolchain upgrade docs and add per-runner upgrade checklist (owner: DX)
Add telemetry: per-runner median latency, remote CAS hit-rate, priming success/failures (owner: Observability)
Run canary on time-windowed queue with 10% of PRs for two weeks, compare metrics, and iterate (owner: Diego)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: splitting runners increases maintenance surface area but reduces cache invalidation blast radius.
Decision: use smaller, language-specialized images with shared READONLY base layer to minimize security surface and image churn.
Priming approach: when a base-image tag is updated, trigger a priming pipeline that replays commonly-failing build graphs and stores hot CAS prefixes.
We will avoid changing monorepo build definitions in this first phase to limit disruption — orchestration will map to existing build tasks.
Longer-term: consider a unified language-aware dependency cache layer, but that is out of scope for this ticket.
progress_updates: 2026-03-11: Prototype node-runner image built with pinned Node 20.12 and hermetic npm ci. Cold-run median reduced by ~40% locally; pushing PR.
2026-03-12: Observability team added CAS hit-rate metric and dashboard. Initial telemetry shows 6% hit rate for cross-language PRs (baseline).
2026-03-12: Security reviewed CAS client pattern; recommended rotating short-lived tokens and scoping them to project buckets. Added Security task.
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Lee): prioritize documentation and DX for onboarding other teams to avoid future fragmentation.
Design (Maya Chen): suggested adding a small UI in Console to show per-runner statuses for flaky PR debugging.
Infra (Kamal Singh): asked to standardize image build pipeline to produce SBOMs for every runner image.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Increased maintenance cost for multiple runner images. Mitigation: add automation to rebuild runners from a shared manifest and schedule weekly security rebuilds.
Risk: Cache priming may not cover real-world prefixes. Mitigation: seed priming jobs with historical build graphs (last 30 days) and A/B test priming coverage.
Risk: Token leakage for CAS client. Mitigation: use vault-backed short-lived tokens and audit logs; rotate tokens automatically.
